rationale:
The structures and most behavior match, but there is a reachability gap for the canonical-project-root constraint.

### Obligations and coverage

- Define `UserAuthoringConfig` with an optional default, a configuration map, and a project-selection map; define `WorkspaceAuthoringConfig` with an optional default and a configuration map that defaults to empty. These are represented by `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]` and `src/config.rs#struct[WorkspaceAuthoringConfig]`. Tests in `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]` cover both maps and project selections; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it]` checks omitted workspace configs.
- Define `ProjectSelection.config`; define `AuthoringConfig.backend`, optional positive concurrency, and optional policy. The reachable types `src/config.rs#struct[ProjectSelection]` and `src/config.rs#struct[AuthoringConfig]` do this, including flattened backend serialization and `NonZeroUsize`. The map-round-trip test above, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]` exercise these properties, including invalid concurrency and policy values.
- Provide both policy variants and their lowercase TOML names; default to Once for OpenAI and Confirm otherwise. `src/config.rs#enum[AssessmentPolicy]` and `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[effective_policy]` implement these. The policy-round-trip test and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_policy_defaults_to_once_without_changing_explicit_policy]` verify the defaults and explicit values. The Bedrock/other-backend distinction needs no additional branch-specific test beyond the tested non-OpenAI path.
- Provide the three backend variants and each listed field: Bedrock model, profile, region, credentials and options; credential access key, secret key and optional session token; Ollama model, endpoint, environment-key name, explicit key and options; OpenAI optional model, endpoint, environment-key name, explicit key and options. These are present in the reachable `BackendConfig`, `BedrockConfig`, `BedrockCredentials`, `OllamaConfig`, and `OpenAiConfig` declarations in `src/config.rs`. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]`, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` exercise their serialized values. Pure field declarations impose no additional transformed behavior requiring separate tests.
- Supply the Ollama endpoint, OpenAI endpoint, OpenAI environment-variable name, and OpenAI model defaults. These are implemented respectively by `src/config.rs#impl[OllamaConfig]/fn[endpoint]`, `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[endpoint]`, `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[api_key_from]`, and the reachable `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[model]`. The backend-round-trip and OpenAI-configuration tests above, plus `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_defaults_are_effective_only_and_explicit_values_win]`, assert them.
- Support string, Boolean, integer, finite float, recursive array, and recursive map option values. `src/config.rs#enum[OptionValue]` supplies the variants and `src/config.rs#impl[OptionValue]/fn[validate]` rejects nonfinite values recursively. The backend-round-trip test covers valid values; `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` covers nonfinite scalar, array, and map values.
- Serialize secrets normally and redact Debug output. `src/config.rs#struct[SecretString]` uses transparent serialization; `src/config.rs#impl[SecretString/fmt::Debug]/fn[fmt]` redacts. The explicit-credentials test above verifies round-trip preservation and absence of secrets from Debug.
- Define `ModelRef` with backend and model; derive it from the selected backend; preserve the exact identifier; do not replace connection settings. `src/config.rs#impl[ResolvedAuthoringConfig]/fn[model_ref]` reaches `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[model_ref]` and `src/config.rs#struct[ModelRef]`. The map-round-trip test checks exact Bedrock identifiers and retention of profile, region, and Ollama endpoint; the backend-round-trip and OpenAI-configuration tests check Ollama and OpenAI identifiers and kinds.

### Gap

The required `Map<CanonicalProjectRoot, ProjectSelection>` is represented as unrestricted `BTreeMap<PathBuf, ProjectSelection>` in `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]`. Canonical-key enforcement exists in `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[storage_rules_reject_each_invalid_field_with_its_setting]` tests relative and noncanonical keys. However, that validation method carries only an implementation reference to `requirements.configuration.loading`. It is not called by any subject-marked implementation root: the struct's derived deserializer does not invoke it. Reading `src/config.rs#impl[UserConfig]` confirms that `parse` invokes validation, but a caller does not become reachable from the marked struct. `src/config.rs#impl[UserAuthoringConfig]/fn[validate]` therefore needs an `{impl}` reference to `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure` (or equivalent reachable enforcement).

No supplied `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap.

text: Habeas MUST define its authoring configuration using these data structures:
configs: Map<ConfigName, AuthoringConfig>,  // omitted means empty
backend: BackendConfig,                   // tagged union, flattened in TOML
policy: Optional<AssessmentPolicy>,       // default: Once for OpenAI; Confirm otherwise
model: ModelId,                           // model ID or inference-profile ID/ARN
model: ModelId,                           // exact identifier, including tag
SecretString = String                         // serialized normally; redacted in Debug
backend: BackendKind,                     // Bedrock, Ollama, or Openai
`ModelRef` MUST be derived from the selected backend configuration and MUST
preserve the exact model identifier. It MUST identify the model without replacing
connection settings such as AWS profile, region, or Ollama endpoint.
Saved configuration MUST remain distinct from resolved runtime configuration.
Serializing and deserializing a valid configuration MUST preserve its semantic
values, including explicit versus omitted settings. Optional fields MAY be
omitted on serialization; defaults and environment-derived values MUST NOT be
materialized into omitted fields. TOML comments and formatting need not
Loading configuration or running a configured feature MUST NOT rewrite the user
or project configuration as a side effect. Resolved credentials and live runtime
objects MUST NOT enter the serialized data structures. Explicitly supplied
credential values are permitted only in the fields documented by the authoring
feature; credentials resolved from a profile or environment MUST NOT be written
Every `habeas author` form MUST assess its subjects under an assessment policy,
`confirm` or `once`. The policy MUST come from `--policy <name>` when given,
otherwise from the selected configuration's `policy`, and otherwise MUST be
`once` for OpenAI and `confirm` for other backends. Under `confirm`, each subject MUST be assessed as
MUST receive a single assessment (including model escalation under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.adaptive`), whose result is recorded; it uses fewer tokens
and less time, such as with a slow local model. An unknown policy name MUST be
rejected as invalid configuration or arguments. The completion report MUST name
the policy used, and each usage record MUST identify it.
